title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE RAILROAD CROSSING IMPROVEMENT PROMOTION ACT
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Railroad Crossing Improvement Promotion Act and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Decree are defined as follows:
1. "Railroad crossing facilities" means barriers, warning devices, control devices, traffic safety signs, and facilities for crossing managers at railroad crossings;
2. "Railroad vehicle" means a railroad vehicle under Article 3, subparagraph 4 of the Framework Act on Railroad Industry Development;
3. "Train" means a train under Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Railroad Safety Act;
4. "Track" means a track under Article 3, subparagraph 5 of the Framework Act on Railroad Industry Development;
5. "Railroad traffic volume" means the sum obtained by multiplying the average daily number of passages through a railroad crossing by trains and locomotives or special vehicles operating on tracks, calculated by averaging a continuous three-day survey on weekdays, by the railroad traffic volume conversion rates specified in Attached Table 1;
6. "Road traffic volume" means the sum obtained by multiplying the average daily number of crossings of pedestrians and "vehicles and horses" under Article 2, subparagraph 17 of the Road Traffic Act, calculated by averaging a continuous three-day survey on weekdays, by the road traffic volume conversion rates specified in Attached Table 2.

Article 3 (Management of Railroad Crossing Facilities, etc.)
A person responsible for the maintenance, repair, and management of a railroad crossing pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Railroad Crossing Improvement Promotion Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as a "railroad crossing manager") shall be responsible for maintenance, repair, and management of the railroad crossing facilities pursuant to Article 3 (2) of the Act.

Article 4 (Consultation on Repair of Railroad Crossing Facilities and Entrustment of Duties)
(1) When a railroad crossing manager repairs railroad crossing facilities, if the manager is a railroad facility manager, prior consultation shall be made with the road management authority; if the manager is a road management authority, prior consultation shall be made with the railroad facility manager.
(2) Where a railroad crossing manager is a road management authority, the manager may entrust to the railroad facility manager duties concerning maintenance, repair, and management of railroad crossing facilities. In such cases, where the railroad facility manager repairs railroad crossing facilities, the manager shall notify the relevant road management authority in advance.

Article 5 (Standards for Designation of Railroad Crossings for Improvement)
(1) Pursuant to Article 4 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or a Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, or Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") shall designate as a railroad crossing for improvement a crossing meeting any of the following:
1. Where railroad traffic volume is less than 50: Road traffic volume is at least 30,000;
2. Where railroad traffic volume is at least 50 but less than 100: Road traffic volume is at least 20,000;
3. Where railroad traffic volume is at least 100: Road traffic volume is at least 10,000;
4. Any other railroad crossing deemed necessary because of a high risk of traffic accidents or to facilitate traffic flow.
(2) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or a Mayor/Do Governor shall designate railroad crossings for improvement under paragraph (1) every two years by setting priorities.

Article 6 (Establishment of Railroad Crossing Improvement Plan, etc.)
(1) A railroad facility manager and a road management authority shall establish a plan for grade separation or structural improvement of a railroad crossing pursuant to the former part of Article 5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "railroad crossing improvement plan") within two years from the date on which they are notified of designation of the railroad crossing for improvement pursuant to Article 4 (2) of the Act.
(2) Where a railroad facility manager and a road management authority establish a railroad crossing improvement plan pursuant to paragraph (1) and improve the railroad crossing, construction may be implemented annually within budgetary limits.

Article 7 (Standards for Grade Separation upon New Construction or Improvement of Railroads, etc.)
Pursuant to the main sentence of Article 7 (1) of the Act, where any of the following applies, the portion where a railroad and road intersect shall be grade-separated; provided, grade separation need not be made where difficult due to topographical conditions or where, through consultation with relevant administrative agencies, grade separation is deemed unnecessary:
1. Where a railroad is newly constructed or its route is improved across an existing road and the conditions of the track and width of the road meet the following standards:
(a) Where the track is single-track: Road width is at least six meters;
(b) Where the track is double-track or more: Road width is at least four meters;
2. Where a road is newly constructed or its route is improved across an existing railroad and the railroad traffic volume and road width meet the following standards:
(a) Where railroad traffic volume is less than 30: Road width is at least 10 meters;
(b) Where railroad traffic volume is at least 30 but less than 60: Road width is at least six meters;
(c) Where railroad traffic volume is at least 60: Road width is at least four meters.

Article 8 (Construction of Intersections)
(1) Where an existing railroad crossing is grade-separated pursuant to Article 6 of the Act, or where grade separation is made upon new construction or route improvement of railroads, etc. pursuant to the main sentence of Article 7 (1) of the Act, the portion where the railroad and road intersect shall be constructed by the following person:
1. In the case of an underpass bridge, meaning a bridge for the railroad where the road passes beneath the railroad (hereinafter the same shall apply): the railroad facility manager;
2. In the case of an overpass bridge, meaning a bridge for the road where the road passes over the railroad (hereinafter the same shall apply): the person bearing the costs pursuant to Article 8 of the Act. Where the road management authority bears all costs, construction may be entrusted to the railroad facility manager;
3. In the case of railroad crossing facilities: the railroad facility manager; provided, where the road management authority bears all costs pursuant to Article 8 of the Act, the road management authority may construct them after consultation with the railroad facility manager.
(2) A person constructing the portion where the railroad and road intersect pursuant to paragraph (1) shall, before commencement of construction, consult in advance on construction design drawings, including elevations, plans, and longitudinal sections, construction specifications, and work schedules with the road management authority if the constructor is the railroad facility manager, and with the railroad facility manager if the constructor is the road management authority.

Article 9 (Management of Grade-Separation Facilities, etc.)
A person falling under any of the following shall be responsible for maintenance, repair, and management of grade-separation facilities:
1. Underpass bridge:
(a) Bridge structures, meaning beams, piers, and abutments, and outer walls within the railroad right-of-way: the railroad facility manager;
(b) Facilities other than those under item (a): the road management authority;
2. Overpass bridge: the road management authority.

Article 10 Deleted. <Mar. 3, 2020>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 25350, May 9, 2014>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 25840, Dec. 9, 2014>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act and Other Decrees for Regulatory Improvement, Including Establishment of Regulatory Reexamination Periods)

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 2015.

Articles 2 through 16
Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 30509, Mar. 3, 2020>
(Presidential Decree on Partial Amendment of 144 Presidential Decrees to Abolish Regulatory Reexamination Periods, etc.)

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.


■ Enforcement Decree of the Railroad Crossing Improvement Promotion Act [Attached Table 1]

Railroad Traffic Volume Conversion Rates (Related to Article 2, subparagraph 5)

Type of Railroad Vehicle | Conversion Rate
--- | ---
1. Train | 1.0
2. Locomotive or special vehicle operating on tracks | 0.5

■ Enforcement Decree of the Railroad Crossing Improvement Promotion Act [Attached Table 2]

Road Traffic Volume Conversion Rates (Related to Article 2, subparagraph 6)

Category | Conversion Rate | Subject
--- | --- | ---
1. Pedestrian | 1 |
2. Bicycle | 2 |
3. Ox- or horse-drawn carts and other things operated on roads by human or animal power | 3 |
4. Motor vehicle — Two-wheeled vehicle | 4 | Motorized bicycle, cultivator, electric wheelchair, etc.
4. Motor vehicle — Small-sized | 8 | Passenger car, small passenger vehicle (15 persons or fewer), small truck (gross weight 3.5 tons or less)
4. Motor vehicle — Medium-sized | 10 | Medium passenger vehicle (16 to 35 persons), medium truck (gross weight over 3.5 tons and under 10 tons), small special motor vehicle (gross weight 3.5 tons or less), construction machinery (gross weight 3.5 tons or less)
4. Motor vehicle — Large-sized | 12 | Large passenger vehicle (36 persons or more), large truck (gross weight 10 tons or more), medium/large special motor vehicle (gross weight over 3.5 tons), construction machinery (gross weight over 3.5 tons)

Note: For subparagraphs 2 and 3, riders or persons pulling the vehicle are included and shall not be counted separately as pedestrians.
